title: Storytelling
idea:
Hypothesis: women 55+ tired of complicated, expensive anti-aging routines will try one ingredient they can keep using every night.
WHY: in 532 comments, the top pattern is women stating their age and "no wrinkles"; 24% use it every night before bed. Most anti-aging products need 6+ weeks of daily use, and a 10-second routine is easier to keep than a 10-step one (our bet, not fact). Proof: Frøya has scaled "ancient remedy every night" for 221 days; our lines/brows angle (#107) is 16% of spend.
WHAT: brand mission: the oldest anti-aging secret, why it works, and Haven & Spool's 10-second ritual.
HOW: documentary VSL with an editorial collage look: real footage of women 50+, real museum archive (Ebers Papyrus, tomb painting), AI female VO, 3 hooks.
TEST: ideation; new angle + new format. Variable: the hook. H1 and H3 = editorial collage, H2 = plain real footage, to learn if the branded look wins.

script.script:
What's the oldest anti-aging secret in the world?

I'll give you a hint. It doesn't come in a ninety-dollar jar.

A real woman ~60 with visible crow's feet rolling our oil near her eye (colour, torn-paper cut-out), with the real tomb painting of women receiving unguent (Met Museum) overlapping as a smaller cut-out. On "ninety-dollar jar": cut to the real-looking $90 gold-lidded jar on a bathroom counter; a hand pushes it away.
script.on_screen_text: HOOK TITLE (serif, on paper), first 5s: The oldest anti-aging secret ("secret" in deep green). Captions start at "I'll give you a hint." Emphasis in red: ninety-dollar jar.

A real woman ~60 sweeps her arm across a bathroom counter crowded with expensive anti-aging products into the bin. Only our bottle stays standing. On "ninety-dollar jar": the same $90 jar shot as H1.
script.on_screen_text: HOOK TITLE (bold white sans, top), first 5s: ANTI-AGING DOESN'T NEED 10 STEPS. Captions start at "I'll give you a hint." Emphasis in red: ninety-dollar jar.

Same voiceover as H1: What's the oldest anti-aging secret in the world?

I'll give you a hint. It doesn't come in a ninety-dollar jar.
script.visual: (Frame attached.) H3 EDITORIAL COLLAGE. Aged paper, serif title. Real macro (colour, torn-paper cut-out): whole castor seeds falling into the open palm of a woman ~60, next to an expensive gold-lidded cream jar. On "ninety-dollar jar": the same $90 jar shot as H1.
script.on_screen_text: HOOK TITLE (serif, on paper), first 5s: What women used before $90 creams ("$90 creams" in red). Captions start at "I'll give you a hint." Emphasis in red: ninety-dollar jar.

script.script: This is a castor bean. Ancient Egyptians were pressing it into oil more than three thousand years ago.
script.visual: (Frames attached.) Real macro of whole castor seeds in a palm. Then COLLAGE: the real Ebers Papyrus (c. 1550 BC) as a torn-paper cut-out on aged paper, slow push-in. Then documentary reenactment, tight and clean: hands wringing a linen cloth of crushed seeds, golden oil dripping into a clay bowl; oil pouring into a clay jar.
script.on_screen_text: Captions. Emphasis in green/gold: castor bean, 3,000 years. Small line on the papyrus: Ebers Papyrus, c. 1550 BC

script.script: And for generations, women have rubbed it into their skin before bed.
script.visual: (Frames attached.) COLLAGE: the real tomb painting and the real alabaster unguent jars (Met Museum) as torn-paper cut-outs on aged paper. Then documentary reenactment, tight: a woman's hand pressing oil into her neck by oil-lamp light, face out of frame. Then a real vintage photo (1930s-50s, licensed stock) of a woman at her vanity. Then today, real footage: a woman 55+ rolling our oil on her face at night.
script.on_screen_text: Captions. Emphasis in green/gold: generations, before bed.

script.script:
And there's actually a reason why.
Castor oil is almost ninety percent ricinoleic acid, a fatty acid that helps condition your skin and hold on to moisture. And dermatologists say moisture plumps up fine lines.
script.visual: (Frame attached: rough diagram only.) Real macro of a golden drop of oil on skin. Then the MECHANISM animation: skin layers cross-section, a thin film of golden oil on the surface, the skin plumps a little and a fine line softens.
script.on_screen_text: Captions. Emphasis in gold: 90%, moisture, plumps up. Small line: Source: American Academy of Dermatology

script.script: But then anti-aging became an industry. Ten-step routines. A different serum for every little line.
script.visual: (Frame attached.) COLLAGE, black & white side: paper background made of tiny serum ingredient lists; a torn-paper cut-out of dropper bottles with handwritten tags (forehead, crow's feet, neck, 11s); more cut-outs of jars and tubes slide in.
script.on_screen_text: Serif title on paper: Ten-step routines. A serum for every line. ("Ten-step" in red). Captions only otherwise.

script.script: And here's what nobody tells you. Most anti-aging products need at least six weeks of daily use to work. And who can keep up ten steps every night for six weeks?
script.visual: (Frame attached.) Clean real-looking footage: a wall calendar, six weeks crossed off one night at a time. A tired woman (55+) at the bathroom mirror late at night, looking at the row of products and switching off the light. Half-used jars pushed to the back of a drawer.
script.on_screen_text: Captions. Emphasis in red: six weeks, ten steps. Small line: Source: American Academy of Dermatology

script.script:
So we went back to the original.
This is Haven & Spool. Organic, cold-pressed castor oil. One ingredient. In a rose quartz roller.
script.visual: (Frame attached.) A hand sweeps the jars off the counter. Then PRODUCT REVEAL, about 0:40: our real bottle, label to camera; close-up of the golden oil and the rose quartz roller ball (Products tab photos / Library "Hand holding castor oil roll-on").
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: Haven & Spool, one ingredient.

script.script: Instead of pouring oil into your hands and rubbing it all over your face, you roll one thin layer right on the lines. Under your eyes. Between your brows. Down your neck. The stone feels cool against your skin. No oily fingers. Ten seconds before bed, and you're done.
script.visual: (Frames attached.) The old way: oil poured into a palm, dripping through the fingers. Then real footage of women 55+ rolling our bottle under the eyes, between the brows, down the neck (Library: angle Anti-aging, action Rolling on). Close-up of the roller ball on skin. Clean dry fingertips. Bottle set on the nightstand, lamp switches off.
script.on_screen_text: Captions. Emphasis in red: pouring. Emphasis in gold: right on the lines, ten seconds.

script.script: And when your skincare takes just ten seconds, it's a whole lot easier to stick with it.
script.visual: (Frame attached.) The same nightstand, night after night: lamp on, bottle, lamp off. A calendar now crossed off in gold, the opposite of the six-week calendar.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: ten seconds, stick with it.

script.script:
Night one, your skin wakes up soft, like it finally got a drink.
Night after night, your makeup goes on smoother, and those little lines around your eyes start to fade.
script.visual: (Frame attached.) Morning light, a woman 55+ touching her soft cheek. Foundation gliding on smoothly. Close-up of the corner of the eye, the fine lines softer.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: soft, smoother, fade.

script.script: Keep going, and your whole face looks younger. And people start asking what you changed.
script.visual: (Frame attached.) A woman 55-60 at the mirror, warm light, small confident smile. Then a phone screen lighting up with a text message: "ok what did you change?? you look amazing".
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: younger.

script.script: And now, over 43,000 women have discovered Haven & Spool, with more than four thousand five-star reviews.
script.visual: (Frame attached.) SOCIAL PROOF: 3 or 4 very quick real UGC shots (about 1s each) of different women 50-65 rolling our bottle on the face or neck. Five gold stars on screen.
script.on_screen_text: Captions. Emphasis in gold: 43,000 women, four thousand five-star reviews. Five gold stars.

script.script: And it costs less than a single jar of the cream you're using now.
script.visual: (Frame attached.) Our bottle next to the $90 jar from the hook, side by side on the counter, price tag visible.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: lasts for months.

script.script: No needles. No ten-step routine. No ninety-dollar jars.
script.visual: (Frame attached.) COLLAGE, black & white side: three wide torn-paper strips stacked on paper (a tired woman at the mirror / the dropper bottles / the $90 jar), each crossed out with a red hand-drawn X as the line is said. Capped syringe only if used, no needle visible.
script.on_screen_text: Serif on paper, red, one per strip: No needles. / No ten-step routine. / No $90 jars.

script.script:
We truly believe the future of anti-aging isn't more.
It's simpler. One ingredient. That's it.
script.visual: (Frame attached.) Our bottle alone on a cream linen surface, slow push-in, warm light; whole castor seeds, a small pool of golden oil and raw rose quartz around it.
script.on_screen_text: Captions only. Emphasis in gold: simpler, one ingredient.

editing_notes:
STORYBOARD: every row has a frame attached showing the look, the hook title and the captions. Follow it.

THE RULE FOR EVERY SHOT: "If AI didn't exist, how would a real brand film this?" Every shot must be something a real crew could film or license. No surreal shots, no plastic AI faces.

TWO LOOKS, ON PURPOSE:
1) EDITORIAL COLLAGE (the brand moments): aged paper background (light ingredient-list texture behind the title only), photos cut out with torn white-paper edges and a soft shadow, bold italic serif titles. Used on: hooks H1 and H3, the papyrus, "for generations" (tomb painting + jars), "anti-aging became an industry", "No needles…" and the end card. Colour logic: OUR side (real women, seeds, papyrus, product) in warm colour; the INDUSTRY side (droppers, jars, "No needles") in black & white. Keywords: red for the industry, deep green for our side. Animate the cut-outs gently (slide in, slight parallax, paper texture), like a stop-motion magazine collage.
2) CLEAN REAL FOOTAGE (the proof moments): routine, morning, results, social proof, product reveal. Full-bleed real-looking footage of women 50-65, warm grade, captions only.

THE PAST = REAL ARCHIVE: Ebers Papyrus (real photo, CC BY-SA 3.0, keep a credit or replace with licensed stock), tomb painting and alabaster jars (Met Museum, public domain). Documentary reenactment shots (hands pressing seeds, oil into a jar, hand on neck by lamplight) only tight, no full faces.

CASTOR SEEDS: whole only. Never show anyone chewing, crushing or rubbing a raw seed on skin.

PRODUCT: our real bottle (Products tab photos). It first appears on "This is Haven & Spool" (about 0:40); in H2 it may stand on the counter, label not in focus.

3 HOOKS = same voiceover, different opening for the first 5 seconds (this is the test).
All three cut to the $90 jar on "It doesn't come in a ninety-dollar jar."

TEXT: hook title only for the first 5s, top of the safe zone. Captions the whole ad, 2-4 words at a time, starting at "I'll give you a hint." Small source lines: "Source: American Academy of Dermatology" (dermatologist and six-week lines); "Ebers Papyrus, c. 1550 BC" (papyrus).

MECHANISM: the attached frame is only a rough diagram. Make a clean, warm skin-layer animation: a thin film of golden oil, the skin plumps a little, a fine line softens.

LENGTH: about 2:00-2:10 at the VO pace. Do not speed up the voice.
TWO ENDINGS: export a "through Black Friday" version and an evergreen version.
END CARD: Buy 1, Get 1 Free / 30 nights or your money back / Link below. Landing page: PDP new offer.
Respect the Meta safe zone (top 14%, bottom 35%, sides 6%).

Voiceover: AI voiceover. Voice: female, American, 50-60.
Tone: warm, calm, a little knowing, like a woman sharing a secret with a friend. Confident, never salesy.
Pace: unhurried storytelling (about 170-180 wpm), real pauses after questions.
Texture: slightly mature and soft, not young, not breathy, not radio-announcer.
Avoid: hype, "ad voice", flat robotic reads.
Pronunciation: Haven & Spool = HAY-vin & SPOOL; ricinoleic = riss-in-oh-LAY-ik.
Two endings: "through Black Friday" + evergreen "So right now, it's buy one, get one free."
Avatar: Hypothesis: women 55+ tired of complicated, expensive anti-aging routines will try one ingredient they can keep using every night.
